fixes.explanation: Close, but it's False. The elders declare, "Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it." They say their eyes did not see it, so they're not claiming to be witnesses. If they had said they saw it, we'd have a whole different case on our hands. Moses tells them to say this while they wash their hands over the heifer (Deuteronomy 21:6 and 21:7).

Right, baker. Moses says the father must acknowledge the firstborn "…by giving him a double portion of all that he has." That's a double portion of everything the father owns. And this is the son of the wife called unloved, so the text is clear that the father can't hand the right of the firstborn to the other wife's son instead (Deuteronomy 21:15 and 21:16).
